terms.scope: OsoSense shows the soil salinity of your plots from the readings of the devices you link, warns you when a reading goes above your crop threshold and lets you record corrective actions.
terms.data: We store your account details, farms, plots, devices, readings, alerts and corrective actions to show you their history. They are used only to provide the service.
terms.measurements: Crop thresholds use the electrical conductivity of the soil saturation extract (ECe), measured in dS/m. The raw sensor reading is not directly equal to ECe; a technical assessment needs the appropriate measurement method.
terms.intro: These terms explain what OsoSense does and how the data in your account is used. By creating an account, you accept them.
terms.account: Use your real details and an email you can access. You are responsible for keeping your password private.
terms.sharing: Only you and the technical advisors whose request you accept see your farms, plots, readings and alerts. You can end that supervision at any time from “My advisor”.
terms.decisions: Alerts and levels are a guide to decide in time. You make the irrigation, leaching or amendment decision, ideally with your technical advisor.

help.eceAnswer: ECe is the electrical conductivity of the soil saturation extract: it shows how much dissolved salt the soil holds. The more salt, the harder it is for the plant to take up water.
help.dsmAnswer: It is measured in dS/m (decisiemens per metre). Each crop tolerates up to a value, its threshold: table grape, for example, up to 1.5 dS/m. Above the threshold the yield starts to drop.
